title: FinTech Business Models: Understanding and Supervising Innovation
summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and firm compliance teams to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their risks.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors, and the compliance teams of innovative firms, to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their consumer, financial crime, resilience and viability risks.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical understanding of the main FinTech business models, from digital lending and neobanks to trading apps, insurtech and crypto on-ramps, and of the unit economics and funding dynamics that drive their behaviour. Participants leave able to read a FinTech's model the way a supervisor does, identify red flags early, and apply proportionate licensing, innovation-facilitation and wind-down tools.
sections.What It Covers: The FinTech landscape and unit economics, digital lending and buy now, pay later, neobanks, wallets and payment apps, crowdfunding and peer-to-peer platforms, robo-advice and trading apps, insurtech, crypto on-ramps and regtech, growth, funding and partnership-chain risk, consumer outcomes, financial crime and operational resilience, licensing, sandboxes and innovation hubs, and failure and wind-down.
Intended Audience: Supervisors, authorisation and innovation-hub staff dealing with FinTech applicants and fast-growing digital firms
Policy, consumer protection and financial crime specialists assessing new business models
Compliance, risk and legal teams in FinTech firms who want to see their firm the way a supervisor does
Learning Objectives: Explain how the main FinTech business models generate revenue, acquire customers and scale
Analyse unit economics, cash burn and funding dependency as early indicators of fragility
Assess consumer outcomes, financial crime and operational resilience risks specific to each model
Evaluate partnership chains and where regulatory accountability sits within them
Compare licensing approaches, sandboxes and innovation hubs and their supervisory trade-offs
Plan a proportionate supervisory response to a FinTech in difficulty, through to orderly wind-down
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with case studies, business model analysis exercises and supervisory question sets, closing with a FinTech failure workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the client's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision, authorisation or compliance in financial services is helpful. No technical or financial modelling background is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, The Use of Supervisory and Regulatory Technology by Authorities and Regulated Institutions (2020)

modules.title: The FinTech Landscape and Unit Economics
modules.summary: How FinTech firms create value, the main business model archetypes, and the unit economics every supervisor should read before judging a firm's viability and incentives.
objectives: Map the main FinTech archetypes and their revenue sources
Interpret customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, take rates and contribution margin
Identify where revenue models create conduct and prudential incentives
syllabus: Archetypes: lenders, payment apps, platforms, advisers and infrastructure providers
Revenue models: interchange, interest, float, subscriptions, fees and data
Unit economics: acquisition cost, lifetime value, churn and contribution margin
Reading a pitch deck and business plan as a supervisor

modules.title: Digital Lending and Buy Now, Pay Later
modules.summary: How algorithmic lenders and BNPL providers originate, fund and collect credit, where affordability and credit risk are mispriced, and what supervisors test in their models and outcomes.
objectives: Explain the origination, funding and collections models of digital lenders
Assess affordability testing, credit models and arrears management
Identify red flags in BNPL growth, merchant incentives and repeat borrowing
syllabus: Alternative data, automated credit decisions and model drift
Funding through warehouse lines, forward flow and securitisation
BNPL economics: merchant fees, late fees and stacked borrowing
Collections practices and vulnerable borrowers

modules.title: Neobanks, Digital Wallets and Payment Apps
modules.summary: The economics of app-based banks, e-money wallets and payment apps, the customer funds and safeguarding risks they carry, and why rapid growth often outpaces controls.
objectives: Explain neobank and wallet revenue models and the path to profitability
Assess safeguarding, reconciliation and the protection of customer funds
Evaluate control maturity against customer growth and transaction volumes
syllabus: Deposit-taking neobanks versus e-money and payment licences
Interchange dependency, float income and premium subscriptions
Safeguarding, reconciliation and reliance on partner banks
Red flags: onboarding surges, complaint spikes and account freezes

modules.title: Crowdfunding and Peer-to-Peer Platforms
modules.summary: How lending and investment crowdfunding platforms match investors with borrowers and issuers, where conflicts and credit risk sit, and how supervisors test due diligence and client money arrangements.
objectives: Explain platform models for lending, equity and real estate crowdfunding
Assess project due diligence, risk disclosure and investor protections
Identify conflicts of interest and platform failure risks for investors
syllabus: Platform roles: introducer, servicer, guarantor or balance-sheet lender
Credit assessment, provision funds and default reporting
Investor categorisation, appropriateness and concentration limits
Back-up servicing and continuity of loan books

modules.title: Robo-Advice and Trading Apps
modules.summary: How automated advice and commission-free trading apps make money, how digital design shapes investor behaviour, and what supervisors examine in suitability, order handling and gamification.
objectives: Explain robo-advice and trading app revenue models, including payment for order flow
Assess suitability algorithms, risk profiling and portfolio rebalancing
Evaluate gamification, leverage and complex product access for retail investors
syllabus: Hybrid and fully automated advice models
Commission-free trading, spreads, securities lending and order routing
Gamification, push notifications and copy trading
Supervisory testing of algorithms and customer journeys

modules.title: Insurtech, Crypto On-Ramps and Regtech
modules.summary: Three fast-moving models: digital insurance distribution and pricing, fiat-to-crypto on-ramps embedded in consumer apps, and regtech providers that firms increasingly rely on for compliance.
objectives: Assess insurtech pricing, distribution and claims models for fair value
Identify consumer and financial crime risks at crypto on-ramps
Evaluate firms' reliance on regtech for onboarding, monitoring and reporting
syllabus: Usage-based and embedded insurance, data-driven pricing and claims automation
On-ramp models: card and bank purchases of crypto inside consumer apps
Regtech for identity, screening, monitoring and regulatory reporting
Accountability when compliance is delivered by a technology vendor

modules.title: Growth, Funding and Partnership-Chain Risk
modules.summary: How venture funding, cash burn and growth targets shape behaviour, and how chains of licensed providers, agents, programme managers and vendors blur accountability for customers and controls.
objectives: Analyse runway, cash burn and dependence on further funding rounds
Map partnership chains and identify who holds the licence and the risk
Recognise how growth pressure erodes controls and culture
syllabus: Funding stages, down rounds, valuation pressure and investor influence
Runway, burn multiples and early warning indicators of distress
Licence-holders, agents, distributors and outsourced compliance
Founder-led governance and growth-at-all-costs culture

modules.title: Consumer Outcomes, Financial Crime and Operational Resilience
modules.summary: The cross-cutting risks that recur across FinTech models: harm from digital journeys, exploitation by fraudsters and launderers, and fragile technology stacks built for speed rather than resilience.
objectives: Assess consumer outcomes, vulnerability and complaints across digital journeys
Evaluate onboarding, fraud and transaction monitoring controls at scale
Judge the resilience of technology stacks, cloud reliance and incident response
syllabus: Frictionless journeys, dark patterns and fair value
Remote onboarding, synthetic identities, mule accounts and authorised push payment fraud
Cloud dependency, change management and outage history
Supervisory data and early warning indicators across the three risks

modules.title: Licensing Approaches, Sandboxes and Innovation Hubs
modules.summary: How authorities licence FinTech activities, the design and limits of regulatory sandboxes and innovation hubs, and how to support innovation without lowering standards or creating moral hazard.
objectives: Compare full, restricted, phased and activity-based licensing approaches
Evaluate the design, governance and outcomes of sandboxes and innovation hubs
Identify the conflicts and moral hazard risks of innovation facilitation
syllabus: Perimeter questions and choosing the right licence
Sandbox entry criteria, safeguards, testing parameters and exit
Innovation hubs, cross-border testing networks and regtech challenges
Avoiding implicit endorsement and regulatory capture

modules.title: Failure, Wind-Down and Supervisory Workshop
modules.summary: How FinTechs fail, what an orderly wind-down requires for customers and their funds, and a workshop applying the programme to a fast-growing firm heading into difficulty.
objectives: Identify failure patterns in FinTech firms and their early signals
Assess solvent wind-down plans and the protection of customer funds and data
Apply the programme to a supervisory case involving a FinTech under stress
syllabus: Failure patterns: funding withdrawal, partner exit, fraud losses and control breakdown
Wind-down planning, client money return and continuity of critical services
Supervisory intervention, communication and coordination with other authorities
Workshop: a fast-growing FinTech loses its funding and partner bank

related.title: Digital Money and Tokenisation for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping banks, payment firms, asset managers and infrastructures decide whether and how to participate in digital money and tokenisation.

related.title: Agentic AI and Autonomous Finance for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms deploy AI agents that act and transact with sound authority, controls, governance and customer protection.

related.title: AI Governance for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance, risk, model risk and technology staff the tools to design, run and evidence robust AI governance across the firm.

related.title: Quantum and Cryptographic Resilience for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms understand the quantum threat, build a cryptographic inventory, plan post-quantum migration and report readiness to the board and supervisors.

related.title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals for Industry
related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving industry professionals and their advisers a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks and controls that matter.

related.title: Embedded Finance, Open Finance and Big Tech Partnerships
related.summary: A nine-module programme for firms building embedded finance, open finance and platform partnerships, covering partnership models, responsibility, partner oversight, data sharing, customer outcomes and exit.
